key_insight: Rarefied hypersonic surface loading does not have one universal influence length: heat transfer is the most nonlocal, pressure is often captured within a few protrusion heights, and shear remains the hardest to identify.
engineering_relevance: For hypersonic vehicle design, this means local wall loads near surface protrusions may require bulk-flow context, especially for predicting heating and shear on rarefied configurations.
method: DSMC data over Mach 4–8, Kn 0.1–0.8, and three triangular-protrusion orientations.
Region-to-point diagnostics using circular neighborhoods with weighted statistics, extrema, nearest-point values, and tangent-normal gradients.
Evaluate surrogate preservation with ridge regression and a closed-loop audit against wall-load profiles for $C_p$, $C_q$, and $|\tau|$.
evidence_signal: Using full-domain descriptors reduced wall-profile errors from 45.5% to 13.8% for $C_p$ and from 72.6% to 12.9% for $C_q$, while $|\tau|$ only improved from 49.1% to 31.9%.
watch_item: The identified information length is quantity-dependent and surrogate-preservation is partial, with the largest degradation in forward-facing heat transfer and shear.
paper_title: Quantity-Dependent Bulk-to-Wall Observability of Surface Loading in Rarefied Hypersonic Flow over Triangular Protrusions
